text:
sam: Heads-up — since the BMC microcode roll last night (batch 2), we're seeing a steady uptick in GPU evictions in us-west-2-rack42. OOB logs show PCIe lane retrains and device resets during boot, GPUs slow-booting or not enumerating.

jess: Which firmware image did we push? canary looked clean. :eyes:

sam: canary was v2.3.1-mc, batch 2 is v2.3.2-mc with the new watchdog throttle change. Canary had 0.2% evictions, prod jumped to ~1.8% after 02:00 UTC.

andre: grabbing dmesg from a node that failed to bring up the GPU. paste below.

andre: ```
[    3.456789] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Device recovery failed
[    3.456790] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: signaled a Corrected error
[    3.456791] nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00.0: pci error: link down, retrying retrain
[    4.012345] nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00.0: pci link retrain failed, resetting
[    4.512345] nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00.0: evicted from gpuset due to hw reset
```

miriam: OOB IPMI shows repeated BMC watchdog resets around the same time: `System Event Log` entries for last boot look suspicious.

sam: infra-oncall-bot opened INC-2026-023 and added affected racks.

infra-oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-023 created by sam: "OOB BMC microcode v2.3.2 causing PCIe lane retrain failures -> GPU evictions (us-west-2)". Affected: rack42, rack43, rack45.

jess: Are we sure it's BMC microcode and not the new OOB switch multicast storm we saw earlier? there were a few ARP floods on the mgmt VLAN at 01:58 UTC.

andre: looked at switch counters — small spike on mgmt VLAN but nothing catastrophic. However, the BMC logs show a flurry of `pcie_link_error` events simultaneous with repeated `oob-net: rx_queue_consume` backpressure. Could be timing-related: BMC watchdog kicks while the host tries to retrain.

sam: test hypothesis: BMC watchdog extension in v2.3.2 shortens the grace period during pcie retrain -> BMC forces soft-reset earlier. That causes GPU to be evicted before driver recovers.

miriam: can we roll the BMC image back for the affected racks? We have rollback runbook but it's disruptive.

jess: Suggest partial mitigation: increase driver retry windows and add an autoscaling buffer on GPU pools for the next 4 hours, so user jobs don't fail hard. Ops can push a soft-rollback to batch 2 only (not full fleet) while infra investigates.

andre: I'll collect more logs — grabbing `ipmitool sel list` and `journalctl -k` from 5 failed nodes and correlate with switch timestamps.

sam: quick correlate output from one node:

sam: ```
2026-02-12T01:57:58Z switch01 mgmt: ARP flood detected, 1.2k pkts/sec
2026-02-12T01:58:02Z bmc-node-42 SEL: Watchdog timeout (force reset)
2026-02-12T01:58:03Z kernel: pcie link retrain start
2026-02-12T01:58:05Z kernel: pcie link retrain failed
2026-02-12T01:58:05Z bmc-node-42 SEL: Pre-reset cleanup completed
2026-02-12T01:58:06Z kernel: nvidia: evicted from gpuset
```

jess: That sequence fits the hypothesis. Two actionable items: (1) Ops: roll batch-2 racks back to v2.3.1-mc, (2) Infra: instrument a longer BMC watchdog grace for pcie retrain cases in next microcode.

miriam: I'm wary of immediate rollback impact on other hardware. Recommend do one rack (rack42) first as canary rollback and monitor for 30m. If evictions drop, proceed.

sam: I'll coordinate with ops. Starting canary rollback on rack42 now. ETA ~15m.

andre: In parallel, I'm pushing a temporary autoscaler rule: +20% spare GPUs for us-west-2 pools. That should reduce job failures while we fix.

infra-oncall-bot: Update: canary rollback queued by sam. Monitoring channel updated.

jess: Thanks — once we confirm, let's schedule a follow-up postmortem with microcode team to discuss safe watchdog timeouts and OOB network jitter resilience. :calendar:
